dedupe_keys.name: life cycle inventories and impacts of european battery waste management scenarios to 2050 eu27 4

description: These workbooks estimate the climate and wider environmental effects of how Europe will collect, reuse and recycle spent batteries between now and 2050. The producers are Harmjan de Vries, Robert Istrate, Valerio Barbarossa and José Manuel Mogollón of Leiden University with Max Tippner and Franziska Maisel of the Fraunhofer Institute for Reliability and Microintegration, working within the FutuRaM research on secondary raw materials. Coverage is the EU27 plus four further countries under three scenarios, business as usual, higher recovery and circularity, for 2020, 2030, 2040 and 2050. The inventory workbook gives the foreground flows for each battery type, lithium-ion chemistry and end-of-life treatment route; the results workbook gives direct, avoided and net impacts for climate change and all 16 Environmental Footprint categories. Both are available as a free download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence, and aggregated stock-and-flow data are in a linked FutuRaM record. Caveats: the detailed material flows by chemistry are confidential and not included, and results depend on scenario assumptions. Simulation uses: planning battery collection and recycling capacity and comparing end-of-life policies in waste system models. Related records: ODYM (model-odym) builds dynamic material flow models of this kind.
